Placement Schemes are independent, reusable records. Rather than belonging to a specific Operative Document, they can be assigned to multiple documents whenever the same placement structure applies.

Placement Schemes

A Placement Scheme defines the financial structure of a Business by describing how premium and related costs are allocated among the parties involved — such as cedants, intermediaries, and reinsurers — through a series of deductions, commissions, and other cost components.

Placement Schemes can also represent businesses with layered coverage structures, where one or more layers define different portions of the risk being placed. Depending on the terms of the contract and its placement structure, a layer may provide coverage up to a specified limit in excess of an attachment amount, and may represent all or only a percentage of that coverage. This allows the scheme to reflect how costs and participation apply across different layers of the Business.

By capturing both the cost structure and, when applicable, the layered structure of a placement, a Placement Scheme provides a consistent representation of how the Business is financially organized within RMS.

This manual explains how Placement Schemes are structured, how their Cost Nodes work, how layered placements can be represented, and where Placement Schemes are used elsewhere in RMS.

§

Before you start: a Placement Scheme is a standalone record, independent of any single Business. It's typically created once and then reused — selected, not recreated, whenever it applies to a new Operative Document. Deleting a scheme that's already attached to an Operative Document is blocked until it's detached.

A new Placement Scheme can be created in two ways: directly from the Placement Schemes option in the Underwritten menu, or inline while creating or editing an Operative Document, using the + button next to the Placement Scheme selector. Both methods open the same creation form, described below.

1 From the menu
2 Inline, from a document

Every Placement Scheme is built from two parts, covered in the next two sections: Structure Details, which establish the scheme's identity, and Cost Nodes, which define its cost structure — the chain of deductions, commissions, and fees that move premium between parties.

Placement Schemes → Structure Details

1. Structure Details

Definition

Structure Details establish a Placement Scheme's identity — the reinsurance agreement type it represents, its share of the risk, and a description of its terms. Together with its Cost Nodes, these details define how the scheme is structured and applied when it is assigned to an Operative Document.

FieldStatusNotes
Structure Agreementagreement_typeRequired*Select the reinsurance structure this scheme represents: Quota Share, Surplus, Excess of Loss, or Stop Loss.
Share (%)shareRequired*Enter the percentage share this Placement Scheme represents. Displayed and entered as a percentage (0–100); stored internally as a decimal fraction — 100% is saved as 1.00.
Daily IndexindexAutoDisplays the sequential number automatically assigned to the scheme among those created the same day. Not editable.
Scheme IdidAutoDisplays the identifier automatically assigned in the format SCHE-YYYYMMDD-####. Hidden while creating; shown once the scheme has been saved.
DescriptiondescriptionRequired*Enter a description of the scheme's terms. Defaults to Each and every loss, subject to the applicable annual aggregate. on creation if left blank.

Placement Schemes → Cost Nodes

2. Cost Nodes

Definition

A Cost Node represents an individual deduction, commission, or fee within a Placement Scheme, defining how a portion of the premium is allocated between the parties involved. Together, a scheme's Cost Nodes define its complete cost structure and determine how the premium is distributed through the placement.

Add one Cost Node per deduction or commission in the scheme. Rows can be reordered, and a running total is kept automatically.

FieldStatusNotes
Deduction TypeconceptRequired*Select the type of deduction or commission this Cost Node represents, from the Deductions catalog.
Sourcepartner_source_idRequired*Select the party the value flows from.
Destinationpartner_destination_idRequired*Select the party the value flows to.
Value (%)valueRequired*Enter the percentage value of this deduction. Displayed and entered as a percentage; stored internally as a decimal fraction, the same way as Share.
GRPapply_to_grossOptionalToggle on if this deduction applies to the gross premium amount rather than a prior net figure. Off by default.
Total deductionsAutoDisplays the running sum of every Cost Node's Value in the scheme. Recalculated live as rows are added, removed, or edited — not saved on its own.
!
Exempt deductions: when Deduction Type is set to exempt, Value is automatically forced to 0% and locked — it can't be edited while that Deduction Type is selected.

To add a Cost Node, click the Add cost node button, as shown below.

Placement Schemes → Using Placement Schemes

3. Using Placement Schemes

The following examples illustrate how Placement Schemes can be created for different reinsurance arrangements and cost structures, showing how each scheme is configured through its Structure Details and Cost Nodes.

A

Standard Retrocession Placement

Standard reinsurance placements may not involve any deductions, commissions, or fees. In these cases, where the reinsurer accepts a participation in the offered risk in exchange for the corresponding reinsurance premium, the Cost Node should be configured with the Deduction Type set to Exempt. This indicates that no deduction is applied to the premium at that point in the placement structure.

1

Example

In this example, Best Meridian retrocedes a 4.5% participation in a Quota Share arrangement covering a USD 5,000,000 excess of USD 10,000,000 layer. The participation provides a proportional share of the premiums and losses arising within the defined layer, subject to the terms, conditions, and limits established in the reinsurance agreement. Since no deductions, commissions, or fees apply to this placement, the Cost Node is configured with the Deduction Type set to Exempt.

B

Captive-Originated Placement

Captive-Originated Placement refers to a placement originated and structured by the captive to cover risks arising from its own insured group. The captive defines the contractual terms and arranges the placement of the risk, either directly or through a fronting structure, including any commissions, fees, and other deductions associated with bringing the business into the captive.

1

Example

In this example, a Captive-Originated Placement represents a 100% Quota Share arrangement covering two liability sections: Contaminated Products, with a limit of USD 10,000,000 each occurrence and in the annual aggregate, and General Liability, with a limit of USD 6,000,000 each occurrence. The premium originates with the Client and is placed through Afirme Seguros, which acts as the fronting insurer. From there, the placement flows through Ocean Re before reaching the participating reinsurer. The Cost Nodes reflect this placement structure: no deduction is applied between the Client and Afirme Seguros, while a 3% fee is applied from Afirme Seguros to Ocean Re and an additional 1.75% fee from Ocean Re to the reinsurer, resulting in total deductions of 4.75%.

✓

A Placement Scheme, once created, can be reused across multiple Operative Documents whenever the same placement structure applies. There is no need to recreate a scheme simply because it is used in a different document. Define its Structure Details and Cost Nodes once, and select the existing scheme whenever the same structure is required.
